subject: DPA annex: segmentation, subprocessor clearance, and evidence roadmap
messages:
From: Emma Choi <emma.choi@healthsync.com>

Cc: Privacy Ops <privacyops@healthsync.com>

Subject: DPA annex: segmentation and subprocessor clearance — follow-up

Hi Sean / Laura,

Thanks again for the walk-through earlier today. As we prepare the DPA annex for legal review, two items popped up from our privacy ops team that we need clarified before we can sign:

1) Segmentation boundary — we need a short (1–2 page) description and a diagram showing which processing components handle PII vs. non-PII and how data is routed between them (edge, inference runtime, telemetry).

2) Subprocessor clearance steps — HealthSync requires the list of subprocessors that will have access to tokenized/identifying data, plus the cutoff (e.g., read-only telemetry vs. decrypted data access) and whether any subprocessor has cross-border transfer dependencies.

Could you share: a) a draft segmentation diagram, and b) the current roster of subprocessors with proposed access levels? If you can also point us at any evidence artifacts (S3 paths or Drive links) for KMS handling and access logs that would speed legal review.

We’re aiming to get this back to legal by EOD Friday (11/12).

Appreciate it — Emma
Privacy & Compliance — HealthSync

Laura / Priyom — couple of clarifying Qs before I draft the diagram: 

1) For HealthSync, do they consider hashed identifiers to be PII? If so, we should mark the telemetry store as "may contain PII"; otherwise it can be labeled pseudonymous.
2) They asked about cross-border dependencies — do we want to list all subprocessors that operate in non-US regions or only those that could access decrypted material? My instinct is to call out any subprocessor located outside the EU/US with potential access, and mark the access level clearly.

Also attaching a short template I plan to use for the segmentation matrix (columns: component, data-types, cleartext? yes/no, access-principals, evidence artifact).

Hi team — attaching the first pass exports: segmentation_matrix_v1.xlsx and subprocessor_roster_20261109.csv. Quick notes: 

- Telemetry store (S3 urn: s3://redwood-telemetry/prod) is pseudonymized by default; raw user prompts are only in the inference runtime KV cache during inference and are not persisted.
- Subprocessors with potential decrypted access: GPU-provider-bid (reserved nodes) — limited to job runtime; KMS provider (key ops) — never sees cleartext keys; analytics vendor (telemetry) — only receives pseudonymized aggregates.
- Cross-border: we have subprocessors in EU/IN/US — only EU data residency requests change routing.

I also uploaded a quick dataflow PNG to the Drive link below for HealthSync to review.

Priyom

Thanks — this is helpful and on a tight cadence. A few items from our side: 

- Please mark "hashed identifiers" explicitly as PII for the DPA annex; our legal team treats deterministic hashes as personal data.
- For the subprocessor roster, can you add an explicit column for "last attestation date" and a short note where a subprocessor has the ability to access decrypted data during job runtime?
- The Drive diagram is good; can you add arrows showing TTL (how long KV cache persists) and where prefix caching might expose partial prompts to the node?

If you can push an updated XLSX + CSV with those three changes by EOD today (11/12), we can move the DPA into our sign-off queue.

Best,
